article.paragraph 1: Edmonton man fatally shot by police identified as construction worker
article.paragraph 2: Vitaly Savin came at Edmonton police officer with knife before fatal shooting, CBC told
article.paragraph 3: The man shot and killed by a police officer at a traffic stop in southwest Edmonton Thursday has been identified as Vitaly Savin, sources tell CBC News.
article.paragraph 4: An employee of an Edmonton home construction company where he had worked, confirmed he worked there as a subcontractor.
article.paragraph 5: Savin's LinkedIn page says he's worked for more than eight years in Edmonton as a drill operator with the company, called Great Canadian. Prior to moving to Edmonton, he worked as a mining engineer in Russia.
article.paragraph 6: On his Facebook page, Savin, 55, is still connected to family and friends in Russia.
article.paragraph 7: A court check shows Savin as having no criminal record.
article.paragraph 8: At around 1:30 p.m. Thursday, Edmonton Police Service received two 911 calls from citizens reporting a possible impaired driver.
article.paragraph 9: A patrol officer, driving a marked police vehicle, located the suspect vehicle in a cul-de-sac near Hollands Landing in the Hodgson neighbourhood in southwest Edmonton.
article.paragraph 10: The officer pulled over the driver. Both got out of their cars. There was a confrontation, the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) said.
article.paragraph 11: The officer shot the man, who was pronounced dead at the scene.
article.paragraph 12: Witnesses to the shooting in southwest Edmonton Thursday have told police the driver came at the officer with a knife, sources told CBC.
article.paragraph 13: ASIRT, which is investigating the shooting, reported in a news release Friday a large hunting knife was recovered near the driver's body.
article.paragraph 14: While ASIRT has not identified the shooting victim, the release said he was 55 years old.
article.paragraph 15: ASIRT is investigating the circumstances surrounding the confrontation that resulted in the officer firing his police-issue firearm and is encouraging anyone with information or who witnessed the incident to call them.
article.paragraph 16: An autopsy is scheduled for Friday.
article.paragraph 17: ASIRT's mandate is to investigate incidents involving Alberta's police that have resulted in serious injury or death to any person, as well as serious or sensitive allegations of police misconduct.
